title: Animated Landing Page: Portal Hero That Parts to Uncover a Full Bleed Image
description: A record label landing page whose hero is a portal: two panels part outward to uncover a full bleed image while the wordmark grows, its tracking tightens and its two halves travel to opposite edges. Below it the catalogue is a deck of sleeves you drag aside to reach the next one. Dark ground, amber and teal pulled straight out of the photography. Good for labels, studios, festivals and any brand whose work is a catalogue.

title: Animated Aurora Background Hero: Dark Developer-Tool Landing Page
description: A dark developer-tool landing page hero with a living, animated AURORA BACKGROUND: warm crimson, coral and amber light-blades that slowly drift and breathe across a near-black #07080a canvas, built as pure CSS keyframes over an SVG-grain texture (no JS needed for the frame). On top, a floating translucent pill nav, a big two-line Inter headline with a warm gradient accent word, an 18px subtitle, two tactile keycap-raised OS download buttons, a GeistMono install caption, and a glassy command-bar / launcher mockup with a typed query, an active result row and keyboard shortcuts. Warm aurora only, no purple. Grab this animated hero background prompt and remix the palette, copy and CTAs for any dev tool, CLI, launcher, IDE, or dark SaaS landing.

title: Animated Landing Page: One Product That Travels the Whole Page
description: A maker's landing page built on one travelling product: a single fixed image of the object keyframed across the opening sections so it is present throughout without being repeated in each one, and a demonstration panel that draws itself at whichever variant you pick, so the page performs the thing it is selling. title: Animated Scroll-Printed Product Page: Warm Cream and Red Editorial With a Horizontal Card Rail
description: An animated, scroll-driven LANDING or PRODUCT page in a warm print register: cream #e7e2d8, ink #171717 and one hot red #ef493c, with Anton set huge and Martian Mono carrying every label at +0.18em. Five sections pin as you scroll. A poster hero whose type lifts, shrinks and fades on three separate variables. A manifesto line that fills from grey to ink through a bottom-up clip-path wipe. A horizontal rail of product cards that travels sideways as you scroll down. A pinned stage where the product's paper artifact is PRINTED in front of you, filling in its lot number, its test result and its dates before a dashed perforation opens across it. A parallax plate whose chapters swap underneath a headline. Every headline splits into per-word spans and roughly 200 elements move independently. Driven entirely by CSS custom properties written from one requestAnimationFrame-throttled scroll handler, with no animation library. Reusable for any catalogue, shop, maker, food, garden or artisan brand that ships a physical thing.

title: Animated Landing Page: Cut-Out Subject Rising Between Two Lines of Split Display Type
description: A studio portfolio landing page where the wordmark splits into two lines and a cut-out subject rises through the gap between them as you scroll. Warm bone ground, one oxide pigment, a high contrast display serif against monospaced technical labels, and a pinned study whose numbers are computed rather than decorative. Good for architecture, design and fabrication studios.

title: Animated Landing Page: Poster Type Interlocked with a Product Photo
description: Animated product landing page where a huge wordmark and the product photograph pass through each other, so the type sits inside the scene instead of on top of it. Two committed colours, small monospaced technical metadata, and scroll animation wired to the product's own mechanic rather than decoration. Good for hardware, audio, instruments and tools that sell on a measured number.

Reusable for any AI, audio, infrastructure or developer product that needs a striking hero with no art budget.

title: Animated Memphis Landing Page Hero (Bold Postmodern Product Site)
description: A loud, playful ANIMATED landing page hero in the MEMPHIS / postmodern style for a bold SaaS or product site. A warm cream canvas is scattered with animated geometric confetti (squiggles, triangles, dotted circles, quarter-arcs, zigzags, a striped circle) that drift and spin via CSS keyframes, behind an asymmetric hero: a chunky bold-grotesk headline with marker-highlight underlines, a violet eyebrow pill, two candy-outlined CTAs (a coral "Start free" + a ghost "Watch the demo") with thick black outlines and hard offset shadows, an avatar trust row, and a tilted product-dashboard mockup (bar chart + checklist). Below: a black full-bleed "Trusted by" logo strip and a three-up feature-card row. Every shape has a thick black outline and a flat hard offset shadow, no gradients. HERO (asymmetric 2-column, copy left / product card right): a violet eyebrow PILL ('NEW - Team plans just dropped' with a mustard dot), a huge Bricolage Grotesque 800 HEADLINE at 76px / line-height .98 ('Ship work that actually gets done.') where two words wear flat MARKER-HIGHLIGHT bars (a mustard bar under 'actually', a teal bar under 'done.'), a ~19px muted lead paragraph, a DUAL CTA row (a PRIMARY coral #ff5b57 pill 'Start free ->' + a SECONDARY white ghost pill 'Watch the demo', both with a 3px black outline and a hard 8px 8px 0 black OFFSET SHADOW that presses in on hover), and a TRUST ROW (four overlapping circular avatars with black outlines + a two-line '12,000+ teams' proof line). The right column holds a TILTED (-2deg) PRODUCT DASHBOARD MOCKUP: a white browser-chrome card (three outlined traffic-light dots + a 'This week - Design squad' title bar) over a body with a 'Sprint velocity' title + a teal '+38%' pill, a six-bar CHART (mustard / coral / violet / teal / sky / coral bars, each black-outlined, rounded tops), and a three-item CHECKLIST (two teal-checked rows + one empty). FEATURES: a centered section (a violet eyebrow pill + a two-line Bricolage 800 heading 'Boring tools kill momentum. Loopa keeps it loud.') over a THREE-UP CARD ROW, each a white outlined card with a hard offset shadow, an outlined color icon-chip (coral / teal / violet), a Bricolage title, a line of copy, and a soft translucent corner-circle accent. Signature system: a warm cream ground, a flat teal/coral/mustard/violet + sky palette, THICK BLACK OUTLINES on every element, flat HARD OFFSET SHADOWS (no blur, no gradients), scattered animated geometric confetti, and marker-highlight underlines. Top: a browser-chrome bar with three outlined traffic-light dots and a bold title. Body: a section title + a colored status pill, a black-outlined bar chart (6 rounded, outlined, multi-color bars at varied heights), and a checklist of outlined rows with teal-filled checkboxes + white checkmarks. Keep every inner element outlined and flat to match the Memphis system."}, {"component": "Outlined feature card with corner accent", "description": "The reusable feature-row card unit.", "prompt": "A white card, 3px black outline, 22px radius, 8px hard offset shadow. Then a Bricolage Grotesque 700 title, a ~15px DM Sans copy line in muted charcoal, and a large soft translucent circle in the same accent bleeding off the bottom-right corner (low opacity) for a playful finish."}, {"component": "Full-bleed black logo strip", "description": "A social-proof band that breaks the cream with a hard black block.", "prompt": "A viewport-wide black #17140d band with 3px black top and bottom rules: a mustard uppercase tracked label on the left and a row of five cream Bricolage 700 wordmarks on the right at reduced opacity. Provides a strong tonal break between the hero and the features."}]}

title: Animated Photographic Landing Page: Scroll-Opened Image Frames and a Circular Iris Reveal
description: An animated, photographic LANDING PAGE for a stay, retreat, hotel or travel brand, in a warm desert register: sand #F0E5D4, deep navy #0B2030 and coral #C64A32, with Archivo at width 74 percent and IBM Plex Mono at +0.2em. Four sections pin as you scroll and the photographs are the motion. A full-bleed hero parallaxes against the type. A framed image OPENS from a small inset rectangle to full bleed as you scroll, its caption carrying a scrim so it stays legible once it crosses onto the picture. A third image is revealed through an expanding CIRCULAR IRIS while the headline over it sits in mix-blend-mode difference. A nightly log advances row by row beside a drawn star field that slowly rotates. Every headline splits into per-word spans and roughly 185 elements move independently. Reusable for any hotel, lodge, retreat, tour, restaurant or property brand whose photography is the product.
promptContent: {"summary": "A long scroll-choreographed LANDING page for a destination stay (built here as 'Ninth Meridian', a dark-sky desert observatory with rooms). Warm desert register: deep navy #0B2030 and #07141F for the dark stages, sand #F0E5D4 and cream #F5EDE2 for the light ones, ink #33291E, and coral #C64A32 with a soft #E2705A as the only chroma. Archivo variable set at font-stretch 74 percent and weight 800 for display, with its ITALIC 300 used for one word per headline; IBM Plex Mono at 11px and +0.2em for all furniture. A fixed film-grain plate at 5 percent sits over everything. FOUR pinned stages, and in three of them a PHOTOGRAPH is the thing that moves: (1) a hero where a full-bleed landscape parallaxes on translateY and scale against a type block that lifts and fades, with a two-stop veil keeping the copy legible; (2) a frame stage where a second photograph opens from clip-path inset(34% 30% round 4px) to inset(0) as the stage scrubs, revealing itself while a large coral numeral and a captioned scrim fade up; (3) an iris stage where a third photograph is revealed through clip-path circle() expanding from 0 to 78 percent at the centre, with the headline above it in mix-blend-mode difference so it inverts against whatever the picture is doing, fading out as the circle completes; (4) a log stage where five timestamped rows light cumulatively beside a drawn star field of 220 points on a phyllotaxis spiral that slowly rotates and twinkles. Then normal bands: a three-column explainer, a rates table of ruled rows with mono figures in coral, and an FAQ. Every headline, lede and caption splits into per-word spans on a 38ms stagger and every row, cell and strap carries its own delay, so roughly 185 elements move independently.", "style": {"description": "Warm desert photographic. Two grounds, one coral accent, and photography carrying the emotion while type stays disciplined. The display face runs narrow and heavy with a single italic light word per headline as the only flourish. Furniture is wide-tracked mono. No radii beyond a 4px softening on the opening frame, no shadows, no gradient decoration except the functional veils that keep copy readable over pictures.", "prompt": "Palette: deep navy #0B2030 with #07141F for the deepest stage, sand #F0E5D4 and #E6D8C3, cream #F5EDE2, ink #33291E, coral #C64A32 with #A83D28 pressed and #E2705A soft. Muted text is rgba(51,41,30,.58) on light and rgba(245,237,226,.55) on dark. Typography: Archivo loaded as a variable font on ital, wdth AND wght; set every display line at weight 800, font-stretch 74%, letter-spacing -.025em to -.035em, and set exactly ONE word per headline in the italic at weight 300 in soft coral. IBM Plex Mono 400 at 11px, letter-spacing .2em, uppercase, for every strap, caption, timestamp and price. Add a fixed grain overlay at opacity .05 with mix-blend-mode overlay from an inline SVG feTurbulence data URI. Ease everything with cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) at 1.2s. Photography is warm, natural-light, fine-grained and unpeopled; never use stock-looking imagery with faces or visible signage."}, "layout_and_structure": {"description": "Four tall pinned stages (300svh to 360svh), each a position:sticky inner at top:0, height:100svh, overflow:hidden, then two normal bands. Every animated quantity is a CSS custom property on :root written by ONE rAF-throttled scroll handler.", "prompts": [{"part": "Parallax photographic hero", "prompt": "A 300svh stage on deep navy. The photograph is absolutely positioned with inset -8% top and bottom so it has room to travel, transformed by translateY(progress * -0.22 * 460px) and scale(1.06 to 1.12), object-fit cover. Over it a three-stop vertical veil (55% at the top, 12% at a third, 72% at the base) so both the nav and the bottom copy stay legible without flattening the picture. The type block lifts 60px and fades out over the stage. Set the wordmark with one italic light word in soft coral. SIZE THE WORDMARK FROM ITS CHARACTER COUNT: font-size: min(var(--display), calc(90vw / (chars * .48))) with white-space:nowrap, because a bare vw fits only the word the reference happened to use and overflow:hidden on the pin will hide the clipping from a page-level overflow check."}, {"part": "The opening frame", "prompt": "A 360svh stage. A photograph fills the pin but is clipped to clip-path: inset(calc(34% - p * 34%) calc(30% - p * 30%) round 4px), so it begins as a small centred rectangle and opens to full bleed as the stage scrubs. A large coral numeral sits top-right and rises from 25 to 100 percent opacity. The caption sits bottom-left and MUST carry its own gradient scrim (a bottom-anchored linear-gradient to 92 percent of the dark ground, at 56 percent height, fading in with the image), because once the frame opens the caption is sitting on the photograph and the ground colour is no longer behind it."}, {"part": "The circular iris", "prompt": "A 320svh stage on the sand ground. A photograph is clipped to clip-path: circle(calc(p * 78%) at 50% 50%) so it grows from nothing at the centre. The headline sits ABOVE it in mix-blend-mode: difference with colour #fff, so it inverts itself against both the sand ground and the picture as the circle passes under it, and fades out as the reveal completes. A mono caption pair fades in at the bottom only after the circle is half open. Under reduced motion the clip-path must be removed and the headline returned to normal blending, or it will be invisible."}, {"part": "The log and the star field", "prompt": "A 340svh stage on deep navy, two columns. Left: a headline with one italic coral word, then five ruled rows laid out as a mono timestamp, a bold label and a muted note, at 0.3 opacity, lighting cumulatively as floor(p * 5) advances. Right: a square canvas drawing 220 stars on a phyllotaxis spiral (angle i * 2.399, radius sqrt(i/220)), each twinkling on its own sine, the whole field rotating at 0.035 radians per second, with two faint concentric circles as the horizon rings and every 23rd star in soft coral. Only touch the DOM when the row index changes."}, {"part": "Per-atom motion budget", "prompt": "Split every headline, lede, frame caption and column paragraph into per-word inline-block spans rising 0.4em on a 38ms incremental delay. Then give every explainer column, column title, table row, table cell, log label, log timestamp, log note, FAQ summary, hero strap item, iris caption, button, nav link and footer line its own data-rev attribute with a --d delay of 40 to 90ms times its index, revealed by one IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.12. Target roughly 185 independently moving elements."}]}, "special_ui_components": ["Photograph that opens from an inset rectangle to full bleed on scroll, with a caption scrim that arrives with it", "Circular iris reveal with the headline over it in mix-blend-mode difference", "Parallax hero photograph travelling against a fading type block", "Rotating phyllotaxis star field drawn on canvas beside a log that advances row by row", "Fixed film-grain plate from an inline SVG feTurbulence data URI"], "implementation_notes": "Single self-contained HTML file. One Google Fonts link (Archivo variable on ital/wdth/wght, IBM Plex Mono) is the only external request. Photographs are base64 WebP data URIs, not linked files, so the page stays self-contained: generate at 2K, downscale to about 2000px for the hero and 1100px for the portraits, encode as WebP, and expect roughly a 240KB total base64 payload for three images. VERIFY THE IMAGES ACTUALLY DECODE by checking naturalWidth !== 0 in a headless pass; a malformed data URI still renders a valid-looking page and passes every layout check while showing nothing. Drive all motion from CSS custom properties written by ONE scroll listener throttled through requestAnimationFrame; read stage progress as -rect.top / (rect.height - innerHeight) clamped 0..1. Under prefers-reduced-motion: flatten .stage heights, make pins static, remove BOTH clip-paths, return the iris headline to normal blend mode, and force all word spans and data-rev elements visible."}

title: Animated Landing Page: Generative Ink Film with a Scroll-Wiped Before and After
description: Dark animated landing page where the background is generated, not filmed. A full-bleed canvas renders ink blooming through water straight from noise, and scroll drives it, so eight sections float over one continuous shot with no video and no image sequence to load. The centre section wipes between a generic default screen and the designed version of the same content. Built for AI tools and developer products that sell on a visible quality difference.
promptContent: {"summary": "A dark, scroll-driven landing page built on one continuous generative background. A fixed full-bleed canvas renders ink dispersing in water from noise rather than from a video or an image sequence, and scroll position drives the field, so eight full-viewport sections all float over a single uninterrupted shot. The centrepiece is a full-bleed before and after: two complete renderings of the same screen, the generic default and the designed version, with a divider that wipes between them as you scroll. Oversized grotesk type driven on its variable width axis, monospace metadata, one accent per section. Good for AI tools, developer products and anything whose pitch is a visible quality difference.", "style": {"description": "Near-black graphite ground with warm white ink and four saturated accents used strictly one per section. The colour never sits in flat fills, it arrives as dye blooming through the background film, so the page changes temperature as you scroll instead of changing skin.", "prompt": "Apply a dark generative editorial style. Palette: ground #0A0B0C, ink #F5F3EF, muted ink rgba(245,243,239,.62), and four accents used one per section, acid #D8FF3E, orange #FF5C38, cyan #6FE3FF, magenta #FF3D9A. Never use more than one accent inside a single section. Display face: a grotesk with a variable WIDTH axis, and use that axis as a real device rather than only weight, 125% for display, 78% for condensed sub-heads, 90% for card names, all at weight 900, uppercase, line-height 0.86, letter-spacing -0.012em. Body in a neutral sans. Every small label, index, spec line and eyebrow in monospace, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.14 to 0.2em, at 0.6 to 0.72rem. Number the sections 01 to 08 in monospace with a 56px hairline rule beneath that scales in from the left. Give body copy a soft dark text-shadow so it survives passing over a bright bloom. Over the background put a static screen-blend caustic pattern, a fixed vignette, and an overlay-blend SVG feTurbulence grain at about 5% opacity, and do not animate any of the three."}, "layout_and_structure": {"description": "Eight full-viewport sections over one fixed background. The cover is centred on a vertical spine, the middle sections pin their blocks to uneven corners, one section goes completely full-bleed with no margins, and two sections hold with CSS sticky while a scrubbed animation plays.", "prompts": [{"part": "Navigation", "prompt": "Fixed bar, transparent, monospace uppercase at 0.68rem with 0.16em tracking. Wordmark left in the display face at width 125%. Links right, each preceded by a middot, at 78% opacity, with a 1px underline that scales in from the left on hover using cubic-bezier(.6,0,.2,1). Below 820px hide all links except the last."}, {"part": "01 Cover", "prompt": "Centred spine, not a left-pinned mast. Stack the wordmark on two lines at clamp(2.8rem,10.5vw,9.5rem), the second line in the first accent. Under it a condensed tagline at clamp(1.4rem,3.2vw,2.4rem) constrained to about 19 characters so it breaks on two balanced lines. Then one paragraph at 46 characters wide. Pin the section index centred at the bottom, and a small rotating circular-text badge bottom right whose rotation is driven by scroll, not by an idle loop."}, {"part": "02 The argument", "prompt": "Asymmetric and deliberately unbalanced against the centred cover. Bottom left, a two-word display kicker at clamp(2.6rem,10vw,8rem) with the second word in the section accent, and a monospace spec line under it. Top right, right-aligned, the section index, one paragraph at 38 characters, and a wrapped row of pill chips that invert to solid on hover. Put a soft gradient scrim over the right half so the right-aligned text holds."}, {"part": "03 The difference", "prompt": "The only full-bleed section, no padding container, edge to edge. Stack two absolutely positioned panes that each render the SAME screen. The lower pane is the generic default: an indigo to violet gradient, everything centred, one type size, a three column row of identical cards with emoji icons, translucent white fills and 1px borders, and a white pill button. The upper pane is the designed version of the same content: the near-black ground, a display headline with one accent word, and three ranked rows carrying a monospace index, a name and a right-aligned note, separated by hairline rules instead of boxed into cards, plus one accent button. Anchor the default content to the left half and the designed content to the right half so neither pane empties as the divider moves. Hold the section with CSS sticky over 180vh and scrub a clip-path inset on the upper pane from 72% to 24%, with a 1px vertical divider and a small circular handle tracking the same value."}, {"part": "04 The offer", "prompt": "A vertical rotated title down the far left using writing-mode vertical-rl. An intro block top right, right-aligned. Three cards along the bottom, stepped up to the right with increasing bottom margins of 0, 5vh and 10vh, on a 900px perspective. Each card: translucent dark fill with an 8px backdrop blur, a 3px accent bar across the top, a monospace eyebrow, an accent name in the display face at width 90%, a description, a monospace spec line, and a footer row above a hairline. Bleed a large ghost numeral off the bottom right corner of each at 12% opacity."}, {"part": "05 The position", "prompt": "220vh tall with a sticky 100vh box. One centred sentence at clamp(2.2rem,5.8vw,5rem) with line-height 0.94, split to words that each start at 0.1 opacity and 0.35em low. Scrub them up and in one at a time across the section, then bring an attribution line up underneath."}, {"part": "06 The index", "prompt": "A two column strip: a count-up statistic on the left with an accent phrase inside it, and six rows on the right. Each row is a display name with a right-aligned monospace note on the same baseline, separated by hairline rules. On hover, fill the row with the warm white from the bottom using a scaleY transform, invert the text to the dark ground, and slide the name 10px right."}, {"part": "07 The spec", "prompt": "Change register once before the close. A short headline, then three columns of dense monospace key-value pairs under a full-width hairline, each pair a label left and a right-aligned value, separated by faint rules. Put a dark linear scrim behind the whole band so it stays legible over the background film."}, {"part": "08 The close", "prompt": "Centred. A display line whose last word is split across all four accents, one paragraph, a large accent pill button whose secondary fill slides up from below on hover while the arrow shifts right, and a monospace contact line with underlines that extend on hover. Give this section its own radial scrim, since the background is at its brightest here."}, {"part": "Footer", "prompt": "A single row: the wordmark in the display face, a one line description, and a copyright, all monospace except the wordmark, over a gradient from transparent down to near-black."}]}, "special_ui_components": [{"component": "Generative ink film (the signature)", "description": "A fixed full-bleed canvas that generates the background instead of playing a video or an image sequence. Scroll drives the field, so the whole page reads as one continuous shot, and it costs nothing at rest.", "prompt": "Render into a small offscreen buffer, about 200 by 113 pixels, and upscale it to the visible canvas with image smoothing on. The upscale is what gives the dye its soft edges, do not render at full resolution. Per pixel: take two cheap value-noise samples to build a domain warp, then sample a four-octave value-noise field at the warped coordinate. Threshold that field TWICE, once tight for a dense core and once loose for a soft outer skirt, and blend both toward the accent colour. A single hard threshold draws an iso-contour outline around every shape and reads as a topographic map. Add a slowly drifting radial bias so a dense bloom is always somewhere on screen, otherwise some scroll positions render nearly empty. Shade the plumes using one of the warp samples so a saturated shape still has a near and a far side. Bake the static water base into a float array once at startup rather than recomputing it every frame. Map scroll 0 to 1 onto the field's z and flow offsets, lerp toward the target, snap when the delta is tiny so it stops redrawing entirely at rest, and gate the redraw on both a meaningful delta and a frame interval. Use an integer hash into a precomputed random table for the noise, not trigonometry, since there are dozens of samples per pixel."}, {"component": "Section-anchored hue ramp", "description": "The dye colour walks the accents as you scroll, and each section genuinely owns its colour.", "prompt": "Interpolate the accent colour in HSV with shortest-arc hue, never channel-by-channel in RGB. Orange to cyan in RGB passes straight through grey and drains the entire page at every section boundary. Anchor the ramp stops to each section's real centre expressed as a fraction of total scrollable height, computed on load and on resize, not to evenly spaced positions. A tall sticky section otherwise has its colour change land a full screen away from the section it belongs to."}, {"component": "Scroll-wiped before and after", "description": "Two complete renderings of the same screen with a divider that scrubs between them, so the page demonstrates its own argument rather than describing it.", "prompt": "Stack both renderings absolutely inside a sticky box, clip the upper one with clip-path inset(0 0 0 var(--wipe)), and scrub --wipe from 72% to 24% across the section with a scroll-linked tween. Position a 1px full-height divider at the same var(--wipe), with a 38px circular handle centred on it. Anchor each pane's content to its own side of the frame, otherwise the pane that is being covered turns into an empty rectangle instead of a comparison."}, {"component": "Character-mask headline reveal", "description": "Every display headline swings up out of a mask instead of fading in.", "prompt": "Split each headline to characters, wrapping each WORD in an inline-block with overflow hidden and each character in an inline-block inside it. Give the word mask a little vertical padding with equal negative margin so descenders and accents are not clipped. Animate the characters from yPercent 112 and a 5 degree rotation to zero, duration about 1.05s, stagger 0.022s, power4.out, triggered when the section reaches 72% of the viewport."}, {"component": "Scroll-velocity skew", "description": "The whole content plane leans into the scroll and settles back to flat.", "prompt": "Apply skewY to the wrapper that holds every section, driven by smooth-scroll velocity, clamped to about 2.2 degrees, using a quick-setter with a 0.5s power3.out so it settles to zero at rest. Because this wrapper is permanently transformed, position:fixed will not work inside it, so hold both pinned sections with CSS position:sticky rather than a pin utility."}, {"component": "Cursor dye bloom", "description": "A soft tinted bloom trails the pointer and takes on the colour of whichever section is on screen.", "prompt": "A 520px fixed radial-gradient circle with mix-blend-mode screen, following the pointer through a quick-setter with about 0.9s of easing so it lags rather than tracks exactly. Give each section a data attribute holding its accent as an rgba value and swap a CSS custom property when that section crosses the middle of the viewport. Only enable it for fine pointers, and hide it entirely on coarse pointers and under reduced motion."}]}

A drawn street network with a route traced to your scroll position. Every headline splits into per-word spans and roughly 175 elements move independently. No images, no animation library, 2px rules and zero radii. Reusable for a courier, logistics, trades, clinic, garage or any service business whose promise is a measurable time.

title: Animated Editorial Landing Page: Condensed Poster Type With Scroll-Pinned Dark and Light Sections
description: An animated, scroll-pinned LANDING PAGE built on condensed poster typography and alternating dark and light grounds. Archivo's variable width axis is compressed to font-stretch 63 percent so headlines read tall and narrow, Space Mono carries every label at +0.16em, and a single orange #FF4D00 is the only chroma against glacier #F2F4F1 and ink #0B0E14. Three sections pin while you scroll: a poster wordmark that scales away into a statement, a numeric ladder whose rows light one at a time as the number counts, and a headline erased upward by a scroll-scrubbed mask. Every headline splits into per-word spans and every row, cell and price line moves on its own delay, which is what makes it feel authored rather than templated. No images, no JS libraries, a generated film-grain plate. Reusable for a studio, workshop, agency, archive, guiding outfit or any craft service with a numeric spine such as a year, an altitude, a depth or a gauge.
promptContent: {"summary": "A long, scroll-choreographed LANDING PAGE for a craft service business (built here as 'Halide', a film archive restoration lab) whose spine is a NUMERIC LADDER. The page alternates between an ink ground #0B0E14 and a glacier ground #F2F4F1, and each section is tagged in the corners with an index and a number from the ladder, so scrolling reads as moving along a scale rather than down a document. It opens on a pinned hero: a full-bleed generated plate of drifting scan lines with a slow orange bloom, a six-letter poster wordmark centred at poster scale, and mono metadata pinned to the bottom corners; as the hero scrubs, the wordmark scales down and fades while a second statement cross-fades into the middle of the frame. The second pinned stage is the ladder itself: a huge year on the left with its last two digits in orange, and four rows on the right that light and indent one at a time as the number steps 1927, 1948, 1961, 1983, with a progress meter along the bottom of the stage. The third pinned stage is a whiteout: a large condensed headline erased from the bottom upward by a scroll-scrubbed mask-image, its caption fading as it goes. After the pins the page returns to normal bands: a three-cell grid of what the service delivers, a four-up row of people each with a generated plate portrait, a tariff of ruled price rows with mono figures in orange, and an FAQ of native details rows. Every headline is split into per-word spans that rise on a 40ms stagger, and every cell, portrait, tariff row, summary and footer line carries its own staggered transform, so roughly 170 elements move independently. All of it is driven by ONE rAF-throttled scroll handler writing CSS custom properties; there is no animation library.", "style": {"description": "Condensed poster editorial. Two committed grounds, one orange accent, and type doing all the work through a compressed variable width axis. Structure comes from hairline rules and 1px grid gaps, never from cards, shadows or radii. Alternate section grounds between ink and glacier and never introduce a third ground. Typography: Archivo as a VARIABLE font loaded on the width and weight axes (wdth 62..125, wght 100..900). Set all display and poster type at font-weight 800 to 900 with font-stretch 63%, subheads and row titles at font-stretch 74%, letter-spacing -0.015em to -0.02em, uppercase. Space Mono 400 at 11px with letter-spacing 0.16em, uppercase, for every label, index, year, caption and price. Radii 0 everywhere. No shadows, no gradients used as decoration, no bento grids, no photography. title: Animated Dark Landing Page: Geometric Display Type With a Scroll-Traced Data Curve and Ember Glow
description: An animated, dark LANDING PAGE built on a wide geometric display face and one ember accent: ink #070908, bone #e9ede6, ember #e44b3c, with Unbounded for headlines and Manrope for everything else. Four sections pin as you scroll. A hero over a screen-blended molten glow field of drifting radial gradients. A statement filled LEFT TO RIGHT by a scroll-driven clip-path. A live data curve that traces itself as you scroll, with a readout computed from the curve so the number and the highlighted row can never disagree. A wobbling molten form that scales up behind a closing line. Every headline splits into per-word spans and roughly 180 elements move independently. No images, no animation library. Reusable for a workshop, foundry, roastery, lab, manufacturer or any technical craft business with a process that has measurable stages.
promptContent: {"summary": "A scroll-choreographed dark LANDING page for a technical craft business (built here as 'Cullet', a hot glass workshop). Ink #070908 ground with #0d1110 and #101412 for the alternate pins, bone #e9ede6 text, mist #a9b5b2 for secondary, and ember #e44b3c as the only chroma. Unbounded 600 carries every headline at letter-spacing -.05em to -.075em; Manrope 300 carries body and 500 carries furniture at +.2em uppercase. FOUR pinned stages: (1) a hero over a canvas of five drifting radial ember gradients in mix-blend-mode: screen, whose opacity rises with stage progress while the lockup lifts and fades, with one half of the wordmark in ember; (2) a wipe stage where a large statement sits at 16 percent bone and an exact absolutely-positioned clone of it is revealed LEFT TO RIGHT by clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - p*100%) 0 0), with an ember rule filling underneath it in step; (3) the curve stage, where five process rows light cumulatively down the left while a canvas on the right draws a piecewise cooling curve, traces it in ember only as far as the scroll has travelled, pulses a dot at the head of the trace, and prints a large readout computed from the curve at that exact progress; (4) a gather stage where three nested wobbling molten forms, built from summed sines around a polar loop and filled with radial ember gradients, scale from 0.72 to 1.22 behind a closing line. Then normal bands: a three-column explainer, a commission table of ruled rows with ember figures, and an FAQ. Every headline, lede and column splits into per-word spans on a 36ms stagger and every row, cell and strap carries its own delay, so roughly 180 elements move independently, all driven by ONE rAF-throttled scroll handler writing CSS custom properties.", "style": {"description": "Geometric dark. A wide rounded display face against a light neutral sans, one ember accent used as heat rather than as branding, hairline rules at 8 to 16 percent, zero radii and no shadows. The only texture is generated light: screen-blended radial gradients that read as something molten just out of frame.", "prompt": "Palette: ink #070908 ground, #0d1110 and #101412 for alternate pinned stages, bone #e9ede6 for text with #dfe4dd as a second tone, mist #a9b5b2 for secondary copy, ember #e44b3c as the single accent. Hairlines rgba(233,237,230,.16) and .08. Typography: Unbounded at 600 for every headline, wordmark and numeral, letter-spacing -.05em on headlines and -.075em on the poster; Manrope 300 for body at 15px/1.6 and Manrope 500 at clamp(.8rem,1vw,1rem) with letter-spacing .2em uppercase for all furniture. Radii 0, no shadows, no photography. Generated light only: draw radial ember gradients on canvas and composite with mix-blend-mode: screen, never as a CSS glow box. Ration ember to: half the wordmark, the process temperatures, the curve trace, the rules, the prices and one button. Ease with cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); reserve cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) for anything that should feel mechanical rather than soft."}, "layout_and_structure": {"description": "Four tall pinned stages (280svh to 380svh), each a position:sticky inner at top:0, height:100svh, overflow:hidden, then two normal bands. Every animated quantity is a CSS custom property written by ONE rAF-throttled scroll handler.", "prompts": [{"part": "Molten glow hero", "prompt": "A 300svh stage. A full-bleed canvas draws five radial gradients in ember at 16 to 28 percent alpha, each drifting on its own sine of time, composited with mix-blend-mode: screen so they add rather than cover; raise the canvas opacity from .55 to 1.0 across the stage. The lockup lifts 52px and fades. Split the wordmark so its second half is ember. SIZE THE WORDMARK FROM ITS CHARACTER COUNT AND THE FACE'S OWN WIDTH: font-size: min(clamp(3rem,37vw,22rem), calc(90vw / (chars * .68))). Unbounded is a WIDE geometric face at roughly .68em average advance, against .44em for a condensed grotesque like Anton, so a vw value tuned on a condensed face will overflow badly here. Because the pin is overflow:hidden, that clipping is invisible to a document-level overflow test; check the line's own scrollWidth against its clientWidth."}, {"part": "Left-to-right wipe", "prompt": "A 280svh stage. One statement at clamp(1.9rem,6.4vw,5.4rem) over 15ch, set in bone at 16 percent. Overlay an EXACT absolutely-positioned duplicate in full bone, clipped with clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - var(--p) * 100%) 0 0) so it fills left to right as the stage scrubs. Underneath, a hairline rule with an ember fill whose width tracks the same progress. Verify the clone's bounding rect matches its base to 0px on x, y and width, or the fill will visibly disagree with the text beneath it. Multiply the progress by about 1.2 and clamp, so the sentence completes slightly before the stage ends rather than exactly at the last pixel."}, {"part": "Scroll-traced data curve", "prompt": "A 380svh stage, two columns. Left: a headline with an ember clause, then five ruled rows carrying a measured value in ember display type, a bold label and a muted note, at 0.28 opacity, lighting cumulatively as floor(p * 5) advances. Right: a bordered plot with a canvas. Define the series as an array of real values and interpolate piecewise between them; draw the full curve once in bone at 22 percent, then draw it AGAIN in ember at 2.4px only from 0 to the current progress, and put a pulsing dot with a soft halo at the head of the trace. Print a large readout in the corner computed as the interpolated value AT the current progress, so the number, the trace head and the highlighted row are the same fact rendered three ways and cannot disagree. This is the difference between a mechanic and a caption."}, {"part": "Scaling molten form and bands", "prompt": "A 300svh stage, content bottom-aligned, with three nested closed forms drawn on canvas: for each, walk a polar loop and modulate the radius by two summed sines of the angle and time, fill with a radial ember gradient at 16 percent falling to 0, and stroke at 34 percent. Scale the whole canvas from 0.72 to 1.22 on stage progress with mix-blend-mode: screen. Then normal bands: a three-column explainer, a commission table of ruled rows (name, muted description, ember figure) collapsing to two columns under 700px, and an FAQ of native details rows with a CSS-only plus."}, {"part": "Per-atom motion budget", "prompt": "Split every headline, statement, lede and column paragraph into per-word inline-block spans rising 0.4em on a 36ms incremental delay. Give every explainer column, column title, table row, table cell, process row label, process value, process note, FAQ summary, hero strap, wipe footer item, button, nav link and footer line its own data-rev attribute with a --d delay of 40 to 100ms times its index, revealed by one IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.12. Target roughly 180 independently moving elements."}]}, "special_ui_components": ["Data curve that traces itself to scroll position with a readout computed from the curve, so the number and the highlighted row cannot disagree", "Left-to-right clip-path wipe filling an exact clone of a statement, with an ember rule tracking it", "Screen-blended molten glow field of drifting radial gradients, drawn on canvas rather than CSS glow", "Nested wobbling forms from summed sines around a polar loop, scaling on scroll"], "implementation_notes": "Single self-contained HTML file. One Google Fonts link (Unbounded, Manrope) is the only external request; no images, no icon fonts, no animation library. Drive every animated quantity as a CSS custom property written from ONE scroll listener throttled through requestAnimationFrame with a re-entrancy flag; read stage progress with getBoundingClientRect as -rect.top / (rect.height - innerHeight) clamped 0..1. Only mutate DOM text or classes when a derived INDEX changes, never per frame, but the canvas may read the continuous progress every frame since it is redrawing anyway. Size canvases from getBoundingClientRect times a devicePixelRatio capped at 2 and re-fit on resize. Note that per-character advance differs sharply by face: budget about .68em for a wide geometric like Unbounded, .60em for a Didone, .56em for a condensed variable grotesque and .44em for Anton, and size poster lines from the real character count rather than a fixed vw. Under prefers-reduced-motion: flatten stage heights, make pins static, remove the wipe clip-path, freeze the curve at full trace, and force every word span and data-rev element visible."}

title: Animated Luxury Serif Landing Page: Near-Black and Ice Blue With a Scroll-Advanced Process Diagram
description: A quiet-luxury LANDING PAGE in a serif register: near-black #090B0C, warm papers, and one ice blue #B9E5F3 as the only chroma, with Instrument Serif roman and italic carrying every headline and DM Sans at weight 300 doing all the small type. Four sections pin as you scroll. A serif hero over a drifting wood-grain field that lifts and dims. A horizontal rail of catalogue items that travels sideways as you scroll down. A four-step process whose DIAGRAM IS REDRAWN for each step, from pulsing rings to a scattered point field with one lit point, to a grid with everything struck through but one cell, to a single settled square. A parallax contour plate behind a closing statement. Every headline splits into per-word spans and roughly 200 elements move independently. No images, no animation library, all canvas and CSS custom properties. Reusable for a broker, consultancy, gallery, atelier, estate agency or any advisory business selling judgement rather than inventory.
promptContent: {"summary": "A long scroll-choreographed LANDING page for an advisory business that sources rare things (built here as 'Coldbrook', a rare stringed instrument bureau). The register is quiet luxury: a paper ground #F5F5F2 with a near-black #090B0C, warm neutral papers for tinted bands, and ONE ice blue #B9E5F3 used only as a mark. Instrument Serif, roman and italic, carries every headline at tracking -.03em to -.05em; DM Sans at weight 300 carries all body and UI; a system mono at +0.14em carries the small furniture. The nav sits in mix-blend-mode: difference so it inverts itself over both grounds. FOUR pinned stages: (1) a hero on near-black over a canvas of 46 drifting wood-grain contour lines with every ninth line in ice, where the serif wordmark lifts, scales and fades on three separate variables while the vignette deepens on a fourth; (2) a horizontal rail of five catalogue items, each a generated instrument-body plate with two drifting f-holes, translating sideways by exactly its own overflow width; (3) the process stage, where four steps light cumulatively down the left while the canvas on the right is REDRAWN ENTIRELY per step (concentric pulsing rings for listening, a phyllotaxis point field with one point lit at a time for searching, a five-by-five grid with every cell struck through but one for editing, a single settled square with a pulsing centre for arrival) and a serif index counts 01 to 04; (4) a closing statement over a parallax contour plate that drifts on translateY and scale. Then normal bands: a three-column statement, a terms table of ruled rows, and an FAQ. Every headline, lede and column splits into per-word spans rising on a 38ms stagger, and every item, row, step, price and footer line carries its own staggered transform, so roughly 200 elements move independently.", "style": {"description": "Quiet luxury. Two committed neutrals plus one cold accent, a display serif against a light variable sans, generous vertical rhythm, hairline rules and zero radii. Nothing is photographed; the imagery is drawn. Hairlines rgba(9,11,12,.14) and .07; muted text rgba(9,11,12,.56). Typography: Instrument Serif at 400 in roman AND italic for every headline, index numeral and item name, letter-spacing -.03em to -.05em, line-height .9 to 1.0; DM Sans variable (opsz 9..40) at weight 300 for body and 400 for UI; a system monospace at 10.5px, letter-spacing .14em, uppercase, for straps and captions. Set the page width to 91.5vw with a 1360px cap, dropping to 89vw under 900px. Radii 0. No shadows, no gradients as decoration, no photography, no icon fonts. Put the fixed nav in mix-blend-mode: difference so one nav serves both the near-black and the paper sections. Ration the ice blue to marks only: an italic clause, the step border, the index numeral, one lit point, every ninth grain line, and one button. Ease everything with cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)."}, "layout_and_structure": {"description": "Four tall pinned stages (280svh to 380svh), each a position:sticky inner at top:0 height:100svh overflow:hidden, interleaved with normal bands. Every animated quantity is a CSS custom property on :root, written by ONE rAF-throttled scroll handler.", "prompts": [{"part": "Serif hero on four variables", "prompt": "A 280svh stage, sticky inner on near-black. Behind: a canvas of 46 horizontal contour lines, each a sine of x plus a slower harmonic advanced by time, at 7.5 percent paper, with every ninth line in ice blue at 34 percent, reading as wood grain. Over it a radial vignette whose opacity is its own variable so the frame closes in as you scroll. The wordmark is Instrument Serif with part of it italic and ice-coloured. Drive the block with THREE separate properties (--hero-y to -70px, --hero-scale to 0.82, --hero-alpha to 0) and the vignette with a FOURTH. SIZE THE WORDMARK FROM ITS CHARACTER COUNT: font-size: min(clamp(3.4rem,20vw,14rem), calc(92vw / (chars * .46))) with white-space:nowrap, because a bare vw fits only the word the reference happened to use and overflow:hidden on the pin will hide the clipping from a page-level overflow check."}, {"part": "Horizontal catalogue rail", "prompt": "A 340svh stage on the tinted paper. Absolutely position the heading and a mono count at the top. Lay five items in a non-wrapping flex row, each flex: 0 0 clamp(240px,27vw,340px), with a generated plate at 4/5 aspect, a serif name, a mono year and a two-line note. Translate the row by calc(-1 * progress * (track.scrollWidth - innerWidth)), measured at sync time so it survives resize. Each plate is drawn, not photographed: a lobed body outline built from a polar loop with cos(2a) and cos(4a) terms, filled in clay, outlined in ink, with two mirrored f-hole strokes that drift on a sine and one ice-blue neck line. Seed every constant off the item index so the five plates differ without any randomness."}, {"part": "Process stage with a redrawn diagram", "prompt": "A 380svh stage on near-black, two columns. Left: a serif headline with an italic ice clause, then four steps as bordered rows at 0.3 opacity that light cumulatively and take an ice left border as the scroll index advances. Right: a square canvas plus a large serif index numeral. THE DIAGRAM IS REDRAWN PER STEP, not merely relabelled: step one draws six concentric rings whose radii pulse; step two draws a 38-point phyllotaxis spiral (angle q * 2.399, radius proportional to sqrt(q/38)) with exactly one point lit and cycling; step three draws a five-by-five grid with every cell struck through by a diagonal except one, which is ice; step four draws a single settled square with a pulsing centre dot. Derive the step index from stage progress and only touch the DOM and swap the diagram mode when that INDEX changes."}, {"part": "Parallax plate and closing bands", "prompt": "A 280svh stage on paper, content bottom-aligned, with a canvas of 26 contour lines behind it (every sixth in sage) parallaxing on translateY -3% to 3% and scale 1.06 to 1.03. Over it one serif statement with an italic second clause. Then normal bands: a three-column statement with serif sub-heads; a terms table of ruled rows laid out as name, description and value with the description hidden under 700px; and an FAQ of native details rows with a CSS-only plus that loses its vertical bar when open."}, {"part": "Per-atom motion budget", "prompt": "Split every headline, lede, statement column and hero paragraph into per-word inline-block spans rising 0.38em on a 38ms incremental delay. Then give every catalogue item, item name, year, note, statement column, table row, table cell, process step, step title, step description, FAQ summary, hero strap, button, nav link and footer line its own data-rev attribute with a --d delay of 40 to 90ms times its index, revealed by one IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.12 and unobserved on entry. Target roughly 200 independently moving elements: stage choreography alone moves fewer than ten and reads flat regardless of page length."}]}, "special_ui_components": ["Process diagram redrawn entirely per step rather than relabelled, four distinct canvas figures", "Generated instrument-body plates with drifting f-holes, seeded per item, no photography", "Serif hero driven by four independent variables including its own vignette", "Horizontal catalogue rail translated by its measured overflow width", "mix-blend-mode difference nav that inverts itself across near-black and paper sections"], "implementation_notes": "Single self-contained HTML file. One Google Fonts link (DM Sans variable, Instrument Serif roman and italic) is the only external request; no images, no icon fonts, no animation library. Declare every animated quantity as a CSS custom property and write them all from ONE scroll listener throttled through requestAnimationFrame with a re-entrancy flag; read stage progress with getBoundingClientRect as -rect.top / (rect.height - innerHeight) clamped 0..1. Only mutate DOM text, classes or the diagram mode when a derived INDEX changes, never per frame. Size every canvas from getBoundingClientRect times a devicePixelRatio capped at 2, and re-fit on resize. Seed all generated geometry off an element index so plates are deterministic and identical between reloads. Under prefers-reduced-motion: flatten .stage heights to auto, make pins static, force all word spans and data-rev elements visible, wrap the horizontal rail, freeze the diagram at its final step and fill the meters."}

title: Animated Landing Page: Dark Console With a Self-Drawing Network Diagram
description: A dark product console landing page whose network diagram draws itself in, then keeps flowing as you scroll. Staggered UI cards, monospaced labels and hairline spec rows, on graphite with a single amber accent and a green reserved strictly for status. Good for infrastructure, observability, energy and any tool whose product is a live system.

title: VOLTKIND — We Build Bold Brands Online
description: A bold, dark, editorial agency-studio homepage: near-black noir #0c0c0c surfaces with a single acid-lime #c4ff00 accent and off-white #f5f5f0 text. A pill-shaped floating glass nav, a massive Anton condensed-uppercase hero headline ('WE BUILD BOLD brands ONLINE.') with an italic Archivo 'brands' in lime, an infinite-scroll keyword marquee, a stat-counter studio statement, a 2-column rounded-card 'selected work' grid with hover reveals, a hover-fill numbered services list, a clients/awards logo grid, a huge centered CTA, and a 4-column footer with a newsletter input. Anton + Archivo + Inter, lime-on-noir, award-site energy.
promptContent: {"summary": "A bold, dark, award-site agency/studio homepage in near-monochrome noir #0c0c0c with a single acid-lime #c4ff00 accent and off-white #f5f5f0 text. Below: a studio statement with a 4-up stat-counter row (120+ / 14 / 98% / 5), a 2-column selected-work grid of rounded-2xl image cards with hover-reveal gradient meta + lime arrow circles (plus a wide featured card and a coal 'view all' card), a numbered services list whose full-width rows flip to a solid lime fill on hover, a clients/awards block with award pills and a hairline logo grid, a huge centered CTA ('Got a brand to launch?'), and a 4-column footer with a lime newsletter pill. The signature is restraint + one electric accent: noir surfaces split by white/10 hairlines, depth from SVG grain and a lone lime/10 blur (no second hue), Anton + Archivo + Inter doing the shouting, and lime rationed to pills, the logo diamond, index eyebrows, one word per headline, arrows, and interaction states. Text opacity ladder on off-white: text-off (primary), text-off/80 (lead), text-off/70 (nav links / footer links), text-off/65 /55 /50 /45 /40 /35 /30 (secondary, captions, eyebrows, muted display words). Use it for: bg-lime pill buttons with text-noir; the rotated-diamond logo glyph; '✦' marquee stars and the footer star; section index eyebrows like '(Studio / 01)' (text-lime, text-[12px] uppercase tracking-[0.25em]); one emphasized word per headline (text-lime); the work-card arrow circles (bg-lime text-noir); the hover fill of services rows; the '+' / '%' stat suffixes; and the animated link-underline. title: Animated Landing Page: Rotating Product Between a Split Condensed Wordmark
description: A dark product landing page where the wordmark splits either side of a rotating product and a pinned section swings a real oscillation derived from the product's own frequency. Graphite ground, one brass accent, a very condensed display face against a wide monospace. Good for instruments, horology, audio and anything sold on a measured number.

title: Pop Art Landing Page (Comic Halftone Product Site, Yellow + Red)
description: A bold pop art landing page for a SaaS product, done as a comic-print website: ben-day halftone dot fields, thick ink outlines with hard offset shadows, a rotated NEW! starburst badge, numbered comic panels for the how-it-works section, and speech-bubble testimonials. A sun-yellow canvas with signal-red and process-blue accents, Archivo Black display type and Inter body. The full landing skeleton is here: pill nav, oversized hero with CTA pair, logo strip, three feature panels, a browser-mock changelog preview, testimonials, a stat band, a blue closing CTA and footer. Copy it for any product launch site, developer tool, or brand that wants loud retro-print personality without losing conversion structure.

title: Landing Page UI (Bold Athletic Performance Brand, Charcoal + Volt-Lime)
description: A bold, dark athletic brand landing page for a strength and conditioning gym, built on near-black charcoal with one punchy volt-lime accent. A giant condensed headline carries the whole voice, and a discipline ticker, a performance stat band, three training-protocol cards, a member PR quote and a free-session CTA make it read instantly as a performance brand. Two type families, flat and photo-free, so it stays fast and easy to remix. Copy it for any gym, fitness, sports or activewear landing.

title: Landing Page Hero: Liquid-Chrome Y2K Product Landing
description: A landing page hero for a modern product, built in a bold Y2K liquid-chrome aesthetic. A deep near-black canvas, lit from within by a soft blue, magenta and cyan gradient-mesh glow, holds a huge liquid-chrome headline, glossy electric CTA pills, and a metallic 3D chrome orb as the hero visual. Full landing furniture (a thin nav, the hero headline and subhead, dual CTAs, a trust line and a logo strip, and a three-up feature row) keeps it unmistakably a product landing page. Space Grotesk display, Inter body, JetBrains Mono labels; deliberately no default indigo/violet slop gradient. Reusable for any bold consumer tech, AI, creative-tool, or launch landing page, and you can copy the chrome-text, glossy gloss-button, and chrome-bezel card recipes on their own.

title: Shader: Aurora
description: A single ANIMATED WEBGL SHADER: Aurora, vertical curtains of anisotropically warped noise. Three phase-offset bands whose x position is displaced by fbm sampled at high frequency across x and low across y, so the curtains stay elongated top to bottom and fall off with height. It is a full-bleed fragment shader with no page around it, about 4KB, no textures, no images and no animation library, and it reacts to the pointer. Drop it behind a hero, a section or a whole page as a living background. Under prefers-reduced-motion it renders one static frame, and it falls back cleanly where WebGL is absent.

The page contains nothing but the canvas. A shared GLSL preamble provides a hashed value noise, a six-octave fbm and a two-level domain-warp helper; this effect draws on them and adds its own body. description: A restrained BLUEPRINT-style landing page hero for a developer / infra SaaS product, built like an industrial spec sheet rather than a marketing splash. A cool slate #eef1f5 drafting-grid ground, near-black navy ink, hairline rules and sharp radius-0 corners, with ONE signal-orange #e4572e accent. An asymmetric split puts a giant Archivo headline against a right column with the subtitle and a primary button butt-joined to a `$ npx forge init` command pill. The signature move is a product mockup card with corner ticks and a measurement rule holding a pipeline run: a stage rail with durations, a stage timeline, a log table, and a signed-receipt block with a perforation and a rotated SIGNED stamp. Closes with a stat band and a mono ticker. Reusable for any CI/CD, build, observability, security or infra-tool landing hero.

title: Shader: Plasma
description: A single ANIMATED WEBGL SHADER: Plasma, four summed sines folded through a fifth. Sines of x, of y, of their sum and of a distance from a fixed point, summed and folded, with only a very light warp so the bands never dissolve. It is a full-bleed fragment shader with no page around it, about 4KB, no textures, no images and no animation library, and it reacts to the pointer. Drop it behind a hero, a section or a whole page as a living background. Under prefers-reduced-motion it renders one static frame, and it falls back cleanly where WebGL is absent.
promptContent: {"summary": "A full-viewport animated WebGL fragment shader called Plasma: four summed sines folded through a fifth. Sines of x, of y, of their sum and of a distance from a fixed point, summed and folded, with only a very light warp so the bands never dissolve. The page contains nothing but the canvas. A shared GLSL preamble provides a hashed value noise, a six-octave fbm and a two-level domain-warp helper; this effect draws on them and adds its own body. Pointer movement raises a smoothed intensity uniform so the effect strengthens under the cursor and relaxes when it leaves.", "style": {"description": "Generative light on a committed ground. Every colour is computed per pixel from a clock and a coordinate; nothing is sampled from an image.", "prompt": "Ground #120210 with accents [\"#FA5775\", \"#FFE5CC\"]. There is no typography and no page chrome: the shader is the entire surface. Behind it a hidden panel that is only shown when no WebGL context can be created."}, {"part": "The shader", "prompt": "Four summed sines folded through a fifth. The same warp as Silk taken through a steep smoothstep and a power curve for near-black troughs against bright crests, plus a filament highlight taken from the warp vector's own magnitude. title: Landing Page UI: Conference and Event Website in Single-Color Oxblood
description: A landing page design for a conference or event website, built as a single-color print poster instead of the usual SaaS marketing page. One deep oxblood field owns the entire site, pale pink is the only light, and all depth comes from a third value of the same red, so the tone-on-tone ghost wordmark bleeds off the hero. Sharp corners everywhere, hairline rules, expanded uppercase display type over mono labels, a pure black event card, a typographic speaker grid with no photos, and an agenda that inverts the whole page to pale pink so the timetable is the most legible surface on the site. Reusable for any conference, festival, meetup, workshop series or product launch event, and the inverted timetable and ticket tiers work on their own as sections.

title: Ledgerline — Deep-Teal + Mint Fintech Startup (Dashboard Hero)
description: A trustworthy deep-teal fintech-startup landing page with a mint accent and cream text: a split hero with a product dashboard mock and a floating virtual card, a bento feature grid, a stats traction band, a security certifications grid, and a glowing CTA.
promptContent: {"summary": "A trustworthy fintech-startup landing page in a calm deep-teal world with a mint accent and cream text. Top-down: a sticky blurred teal nav, a split hero (left: a NEW-yield pill, a big 'Finance built for the speed of a startup' headline with the last word in mint, sub-copy, dual CTAs and a trust row; right: a glassy product dashboard mock showing an operating-account balance, a mint area chart and auto-categorized transactions, with a tilted virtual-card chip floating off the corner), a centered 'trusted by' compliance logo strip, a bento feature grid mixing wide and tall cards with inline product mocks (send-money, receipt-matching, per-card controls, accounting sync), a stats / traction band of four big mint figures plus a pull-quote, a security & compliance section with a certifications badge grid (SOC 2 / PCI / GDPR / ISO), a glowing centered CTA, and a four-column footer. A soft mint radial 'grain' glow sits behind the hero, traction band and CTA.", "style": {"description": "Calm, premium fintech aesthetic built on deep teal surfaces, a single mint accent, and warm cream text. The whole page lives on teal-900 #0f3d3e with darker teal-950 #0a2a2b panels and lighter teal-800 #134847 / teal-700 #1b5a58 card fills; the one accent is mint #4fd1c5 (used for the logo mark, primary buttons, the chart line, positive numbers, check marks, eyebrows and tinted icon tiles), and all text is cream #eef5f0 at varying opacities. Surfaces read as soft frosted glass via thin inset cream hairline 'rings' (inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(238,245,240,0.08)) and deep ambient drop shadows rather than hard borders. A reusable mint 'grain' backdrop (layered radial mint glows + a subtle top vertical wash) sits behind the hero, traction band and CTA. Trust, calm, and clarity over flash: lots of breathing room, tabular-numeric figures for money, gentle hover tints, no harsh contrast.", "prompt": "Build a calm, trustworthy fintech look. Background is teal-900 #0f3d3e; panels and the darkest surfaces use teal-950 #0a2a2b, card fills use teal-800 #134847 and the floating card chip uses a teal-700 #1b5a58 -> teal-800 gradient. The single accent is mint #4fd1c5: use it for the logo mark, primary pill buttons (mint fill, teal-950 #0a2a2b text), the area-chart stroke and gradient, positive/credit amounts, check marks, eyebrow labels, tinted icon tiles (mint at ~12-15% opacity behind a mint glyph) and 'Live' status dots. All text is cream #eef5f0: headings at full strength, body at ~65-70% (cream/65-70), muted meta at ~60%. Treat every surface as soft frosted glass: instead of hard borders use a 1px inset cream hairline ring `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(238,245,240,0.08)` plus deep ambient shadows (cards: 0 24px 60px -28px rgba(0,0,0,0.7); the dashboard mock: 0 40px 90px -40px rgba(0,0,0,0.75)); primary buttons get a soft mint glow `0 10px 30px -10px rgba(79,209,197,0.5)`. Reusable 'grain' backdrop = layered radial gradients: a strong mint bloom rgba(79,209,197,0.18) at 82% -12%, a faint mint bloom rgba(79,209,197,0.07) at 6% 4%, over a subtle top-down teal wash; reuse it behind the hero, the traction band (at ~70% opacity) and the CTA (plus a big mint blur orb). title: Shader: Metaballs
description: A single ANIMATED WEBGL SHADER: Metaballs, a summed inverse-square field, thresholded. Five centres on de-synchronised orbits each contribute a small charge over squared distance; the surface is where the sum crosses a threshold, which is why the forms merge and separate like liquid. It is a full-bleed fragment shader with no page around it, about 4KB, no textures, no images and no animation library, and it reacts to the pointer. Drop it behind a hero, a section or a whole page as a living background. Under prefers-reduced-motion it renders one static frame, and it falls back cleanly where WebGL is absent.

title: Shader: Caustics
description: A single ANIMATED WEBGL SHADER: Caustics, the interference of three travelling wave sources. Three sine sources drift on their own orbits; their summed phase is ridged with an absolute value and a power curve, which is what turns interference into the bright filigree you see on a pool floor. It is a full-bleed fragment shader with no page around it, about 4KB, no textures, no images and no animation library, and it reacts to the pointer. Drop it behind a hero, a section or a whole page as a living background. Under prefers-reduced-motion it renders one static frame, and it falls back cleanly where WebGL is absent.

Three sine sources drift on their own orbits; their summed phase is ridged with an absolute value and a power curve, which is what turns interference into the bright filigree you see on a pool floor. The page contains nothing but the canvas. A shared GLSL preamble provides a hashed value noise, a six-octave fbm and a two-level domain-warp helper; this effect draws on them and adds its own body. Pointer movement raises a smoothed intensity uniform so the effect strengthens under the cursor and relaxes when it leaves.", "style": {"description": "Generative light on a committed ground. Behind it a hidden panel that is only shown when no WebGL context can be created."}, {"part": "The shader", "prompt": "The interference of three travelling wave sources. Without the ridge the sum reads as soft banding rather than caustics. Build one WebGL program, draw two triangles, and pass resolution, time and an intensity uniform. Cap the drawing buffer below device pixel ratio (this one uses 0.85 to 0.95 of a 1.5x cap) because two-level warping costs about 18 noise samples per pixel. Verification note: readPixels on a live WebGL canvas returns zeros because it reads the back buffer after present, so judge from a rendered screenshot rather than sampled pixels."}

title: Landing Page UI: Event Ticket Website Where Your Name Is Laser-Cut Into a Metal Pass
description: An event ticketing landing page where the pass is a laser-etched metal plate instead of a paper ticket. Type your name straight into the plate and the cutter stops at the plate's edge, because the field is 20 characters wide and metal does not stretch. Every plate on the page is live, it is pure HTML and CSS with no JavaScript, and the whole thing runs off one millimetre custom property so the spec printed on the page is literally the spec drawing it. A good starting point for any event, ticketing, festival or credential landing page that needs a real point of view instead of a hero image and a tier table.

description: A premium DARK developer-tool / B2B-SaaS landing-page hero on a cool near-black #0a0c10 canvas with ONE flat electric-cyan #22d3ee accent as the only chroma (no gradient, no glow). title: All Kits. Take Your Pick. — LumenStudio Kit Carousel
description: A light, Apple-Shop-style product-card carousel: a horizontal scroll-snap track of tall white kit cards (the first highlighted with a 'New' badge + cobalt ring + lift, the next peeking past the right edge), circular prev/next arrows, color-swatch dots, and a thin cobalt progress bar with an 01/06 counter, all on near-white surfaces with a single cobalt-blue accent and Inter type.
promptContent: {"summary": "A light, premium product page for an AI design agent's design-hardware brand ('LumenStudio'), anchored by an Apple-Shop-style PRODUCT-CARD CAROUSEL: a horizontal, scroll-snapping track of tall white kit cards, the first card highlighted (a 'New' badge, a cobalt ring, and a stronger lifted shadow) and a fourth card peeking in from the right edge to signal more. Each card carries an oversized extrabold product name, a soft tinted radial 'grain' tile holding a stylized device mock, a row of color-swatch dots, a one-line descriptor, and a 'From $price / kit' + Buy footer split by a hairline. Sections (a sticky blurred nav, a full-bleed hero strip 'All kits. Take your pick.', the carousel section with a header row + circular prev/next arrows + a thin progress bar with an 01/06 counter, and a full-bleed shipping/compare footer strip) all sit inside a centered max-w-[1180px] column and reflow to a draggable single-row track on mobile.", "style": {"description": "Light, airy, premium Apple-store-like commerce UI. Surfaces are a paper near-white (#f8fafc) page over pure-white (#ffffff) cards and nav; ink text is a near-black navy (#0b1220) for headings with a slate 'slatey' (#475569) for body/secondary. A single cobalt-blue accent runs through the logo tile, the primary buttons, the active card's ring, the next arrow, and the progress fill (cobalt-500 #2563eb primary, cobalt-600 #1d4ed8 hover, cobalt-700 #1e40af deep, with tints cobalt-50 #eff4ff and cobalt-100 #dbe6ff for badges/rings). Per-card device mocks introduce playful secondary product hues (sky, violet, emerald, orange-400) used ONLY inside the device tiles and as swatch dots, never on chrome. Depth is soft and quiet: named shadows card = 0 1px 2px rgba(15,23,42,.04), 0 12px 30px -12px rgba(15,23,42,.18); cardhi = 0 2px 4px rgba(15,23,42,.06), 0 28px 50px -18px rgba(37,99,235,.30) (a cobalt-tinted lift on the highlighted card); nav = 0 1px 0 rgba(15,23,42,.06); and a pill glow = 0 6px 18px -6px rgba(37,99,235,.55) on cobalt buttons. Borders are slate-200 hairlines (and ring-1 cobalt-100 on the active card); a device drop-shadow filter (drop-shadow(0 26px 30px rgba(15,23,42,.18))) floats the mocks. Corners are generously rounded: rounded-full pills/arrows, rounded-[26px] cards, rounded-[20px] device tiles, rounded-[9px]/[18px]/[14px] device bodies. Soft radial 'grain' gradients (white -> faint blue/slate) sit behind hero and inside each device tile. Type is Inter throughout (400-900), with extrabold tracking-tight display headings, an uppercase wide-tracked ([0.16em]) cobalt eyebrow, and relaxed slatey body copy.", "prompt": "Design a light, premium, Apple-store-like commerce UI. Palette EXACTLY: page background paper #f8fafc with pure-white #ffffff cards and nav; text ink #0b1220 (near-black navy) for headings and 'slatey' #475569 for body/secondary/nav links; single accent cobalt-blue with cobalt-500 #2563eb as the primary, cobalt-600 #1d4ed8 as hover, cobalt-700 #1e40af as the deep stop in gradients, and tints cobalt-50 #eff4ff and cobalt-100 #dbe6ff for badges, rings, and active-card backgrounds. Reserve playful secondary product hues (sky-100/300, violet-200/300, emerald-200/300/400/500, orange-400) ONLY for the per-card device mocks and the small color-swatch dots, never on nav/buttons/chrome. description: A dark LANDING PAGE UI for a stage and event lighting studio with a colour system you can prove: the page is a dark stage (#14132b) lit by two lamps, a magenta gel #F42FCB and a cyan gel #1CB0F6, and every colour on it is one of the lamps, the pale orchid the two beams make where they physically cross (a real CSS mix-blend-mode screen overlap, computed by the browser, never hand painted), dim white for unlit things, or pure white meaning all the lamps are on. title: Prismline — Aurora Glass: Ship a SaaS Site That Looks Designed, Not Generated
description: A premium dark aurora-glass SaaS marketing site: frosted pill nav, duotone aqua-to-magenta hero, a floating infinite-canvas mockup, a 6-card feature grid, bento showcase, 3-tier pricing with a featured Pro plan, and a glass footer.
promptContent: {"summary": "Build a premium dark glassmorphic SaaS marketing site for 'Prismline' on a near-black page (#0b0f14) lit by soft aqua-to-magenta aurora blobs. A sticky frosted-glass pill nav floats over a centered hero with duotone gradient text, a floating frosted dashboard-canvas mockup, a logo strip, a 6-card feature grid, a bento showcase, a 3-tier pricing block with a featured Pro plan, a big glass CTA, and a 5-column glass footer.", "style": {"description": "Dark aurora-glass aesthetic: a single near-black canvas under soft, blurred aqua and magenta light fields, with frosted translucent panels, hairline borders, and duotone aqua-to-magenta gradient accents on headings, badges and buttons. Premium, luminous, restrained: glass surfaces never go opaque, accents stay in the aqua/cyan/magenta family only (no generic indigo or violet).", "prompt": "Palette: page base #0b0f14 (also the dark button label color), body text #e7ecf2 with muted whites (white/65, white/55, white/45, white/35). Accent family only: aqua #2dd4bf, aqua-soft #5eead4, cyan #22d3ee, magenta #e879f9. Frosted glass surfaces: .glass = linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.07), rgba(255,255,255,0.02)) with backdrop-filter blur(18px) saturate(140%) and a 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.10) border; .glass-strong = linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.10), rgba(255,255,255,0.03)) with blur(26px) saturate(150%) and a 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.14) border. Duotone gradient text (.duo-text) = linear-gradient(100deg, #2dd4bf 0%, #5eead4 35%, #e879f9 100%) clipped to text. Primary CTA buttons = linear-gradient(135deg, #5eead4, #2dd4bf) with #0b0f14 label text; secondary = glass with white/80 text. Aurora blobs = large blurred (filter blur(90px)) ~0.2-0.55 opacity circles of #2dd4bf, #e879f9 and #22d3ee scattered behind sections. Subtle 56px x 56px grid texture (rgba(255,255,255,0.04) lines) radially masked at section tops, plus a faint fractal-noise overlay at ~0.035 opacity. Gradient ring borders use a 135deg aqua->magenta mask trick. Fonts via Google Fonts: Space Grotesk (display, weights 400-700) for the wordmark, all headings, badges and buttons; Inter (body, weights 400-700) for paragraphs and lists. Tight display tracking, leading ~1.02 on the big hero. Mood: premium, frosted, luminous-on-dark; antialiased."}, "layout_and_structure": {"description": "A single full-width responsive marketing page, max-w-6xl centered container with px-5/px-6, stacked sections separated by generous top padding (pt-24 / sm:pt-32). title: Landing Page UI: Online Course Website Where Finished Modules Peel Off a Sticker Sheet
description: A course landing page UI where the curriculum is a die-cut STICKER SHEET — an online course website design on a blush pink ground where every student is mailed the 8 modules as kiss-cut stickers: finish a module, peel its sticker, press it on your laptop lid. The hero shows a finished student's sheet (8 empty dated wells) next to her laptop lid carrying all 8 peeled stickers; the curriculum section is the fresh sheet itself, a cream backing panel with 8 same-size module stickers in a crimson/cream two-tone checkerboard, each ringed by a dashed kiss-cut contour, the first sticker's corner lifted. Three material states replace every progress bar: intact sticker (module ahead), lifted corner (peel next), empty dated well (finished). Navy League Spartan headline, Poppins everywhere else, one arced-text instructor seal, navy enroll band. Reusable for any course, curriculum, bootcamp, or milestone-based product landing page.
promptContent: {"summary": "A marketing LANDING PAGE for an online course whose signature is a physical, mailed KISS-CUT STICKER SHEET curriculum, built entirely out of that material system on a blush pink #f3c9d5 ground with deep navy #1A2540 ink, crimson #cc2b3f accent, and cream #f2e9db backing paper. The page's repeating unit is a sticker's MATERIAL STATE: an INTACT sticker (a chunky rounded badge ringed by a thin dashed kiss-cut contour) means a module still ahead; a LIFTED CORNER (a folded CSS triangle with a hatched shadow under it) means the module you peel next; an EMPTY WELL (the dashed ring with a faint silhouette on the backing, printing the module name and a peel date) means finished. The curriculum section IS the fresh sheet: a cream backing panel with a soft shadow floating on the blush ground, holding 8 same-size module stickers in a 4x2 grid (2-up on mobile), alternating crimson-filled (cream text) and cream-tint (crimson text and a printed crimson ring) in a checkerboard, each carrying a big numeral, a simple line icon, the module name and its duration, with sticker 01's corner pre-lifted. Below: a three-state 'how your sheet works' legend, one arced-text SVG roundel instructor seal, and a navy enroll band with a single crimson pill button. Flat print-like color, no gradients (only two hard-stop patterns: the corner fold and the hatch), no photos, fully responsive.", "style": {"description": "Print-shop material design: the page reads as a real sticker sheet product, not a themed illustration. The kiss-cut dashed contour, the folded lifted corner, the hatched peel shadow and the dated empty wells are the entire ornament vocabulary; there are no gradients, no glows, no photos. League Spartan 800 carries the navy headlines; Poppins does everything else. Express progress ONLY through material states: intact sticker, lifted folded corner with a hatched shadow, or an empty dashed well with a faint silhouette and a printed peel date on the backing. Left side: a small crimson eyebrow, a two-line navy League Spartan headline, a one-sentence subline explaining the mailed sticker-sheet curriculum, and a bordered stat chip with module count, exact total duration and 'peel as you go'. Alternate crimson-filled stickers (cream print) with cream-tint stickers (crimson print and a 2px printed crimson ring) in a checkerboard. Give sticker 01 a lifted corner: a folded triangle made with a hard-stop CSS gradient plus a hatched shadow peeking from under the fold.
